call last_turn_provider(conn, 'proj-1', 'conv-1')
cases.notes: SELECT ... WHERE provider IS NOT NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 — the most recently created row with a non-NULL provider wins, which is how a resume token left behind by a different CLI (after the chat's routing changed) is detected by claude_cmd::session_for_provider.

call last_turn_provider(conn, 'proj-1', 'conv-inexistente')
cases.notes: Rows written before provider tracking existed have provider = NULL, which the WHERE provider IS NOT NULL filter excludes entirely, so the query returns no row rather than a NULL value. The caller reads None as 'can't tell' and keeps whatever session it already had, rather than discarding a working one. A conversation id with zero rows produces the identical None, so the two cases are indistinguishable from this function's return alone.

call get_conversation_messages(conn, 'proj-1', 'conv-1')
take the last non-null engine_session_id among the returned turns, oldest first
cases.notes: get_conversation_messages orders ASC by created_at (oldest first) so the frontend can flatten turns directly into [user, assistant, user, assistant, ...]. Reopening a conversation must resume the engine session of its LATEST turn, i.e. the last element's engine_session_id, not the first.
